claims.text: The powder feedstock is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi.
The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock was produced via conventional L-PBF.
Conventionally L-PBF-processed AlCrFeNiSi typically exhibits compositional segregation during cooling.
Conventionally L-PBF-processed AlCrFeNiSi typically has high residual thermal stresses.
Conventionally L-PBF-processed AlCrFeNiSi typically has an elevated density of processing defects.
The proposed closed-loop system will use in-situ thermal feedback to adjust laser power and scan speed in real time.
Laser power and scan speed are consequential L-PBF process parameters that influence build quality and defect formation in high-entropy alloys.
Dynamic adjustment of laser parameters will create a controlled, locally tailored cooling profile.
The tailored cooling profile will produce a finer and more uniform microstructure.
The tailored cooling profile will minimize phase or compositional segregation.
The tailored cooling profile will minimize residual-stress gradients.
Real-time thermal-feedback control will reduce defect formation during rapid solidification.
ML-controlled AlCrFeNiSi will have fewer pores and cracks than fixed-parameter L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
ML-controlled AlCrFeNiSi will have lower residual stress than fixed-parameter L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
ML-controlled AlCrFeNiSi will be more compositionally homogeneous than fixed-parameter L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
ML-controlled AlCrFeNiSi will have higher yield strength than fixed-parameter L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
ML-controlled AlCrFeNiSi will have higher ductility than fixed-parameter L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
The intervention is expected to remain effective across typical L-PBF energy-density and cooling-rate ranges for AlCrFeNiSi.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field says the powder feedstock itself was produced via conventional L-PBF, whereas the intervention and baseline correctly treat powder as the input used by L-PBF to manufacture samples. This creates an internally inconsistent description of the material's processing state.
